name: Pearl Oyster: baby clusters
summary: Lots of fresh air and an early pick for small, thick caps on short stems. The tender clusters restaurants serve whole.
notes: Pick the whole cluster while the cap edges still roll under, before any flatten. Expect a lighter harvest than a full-size grow.
chamber_notes: Chamber limits: there is no heater or cooler, so temperature targets only hold if the room sits near them. There is no CO2 sensor, so the fan schedule stands in for fresh air. The humidifier can only add moisture, so a low humidity target depends on dry room air.

source_notes.title: MushWorld 2004, oyster abnormalities
source_notes.detail: Mushroom Growers' Handbook 1, ch. 8, MushWorld 2004. P. ostreatus fruits best at 13 to 16 °C and over 80% RH. Low temperature with high humidity gives strong color and firm fruits that grow slowly; high temperature gives lighter caps. At 0.03% CO2 caps were 6.5 mm with 4.6 mm stipes; at 0.1% caps were 3.4 mm with 6.8 mm stipes. Too much air movement also deforms fruits.

source_notes.title: FungiAlly oyster booklet, SARE
source_notes.detail: FungiAlly, oyster mushroom production booklet, SARE project. Fruiting at 85 to 90% RH with CO2 below 800 ppm. Harvest 5 to 10 days into fruiting, before the cap edges flatten. A slight roll on the edge keeps texture and storage life. High CO2 gives long stems and little caps.

source_notes.title: Stamets
source_notes.detail: Paul Stamets, Growing Gourmet and Medicinal Mushrooms (commonly cited chamber ranges). P. ostreatus spawn run ~24 °C; fruiting often 10 to 21 °C at 85 to 90% humidity.

stages.name: Colonization
stages.notes: Dark, little fresh air until the block is white.

stages.name: Pinning
stages.notes: Drop temperature and add fresh air to trigger clusters.

stages.name: Baby fruiting
stages.notes: Strong but not maximum air. Too much air movement also deforms fruits.

light_recipe.why: Light stays at the free card default. This profile changes air and timing, not light.
light_recipe.wavelength_note: WS2812 red is roughly 620 to 630 nm and blue roughly 465 to 475 nm. The RGB mix is an approximation of the cited wavelengths, not a measured spectrum. RGB percent is LED drive level, not a photon ratio.

sources.title: Penn State oyster production
sources.detail: Daniel J. Royse, Cultivation of Oyster Mushrooms, Penn State College of Agricultural Sciences. First 12 to 21 days of spawn run may be completed without artificial lighting. After spawn run, 4 h of cool white fluorescent light at 50 to 300 lux may be provided. This recipe uses 12 h as a labeled default photoperiod, not a page-cited Stamets value, and maps 20% white to 92 lux, inside that 50 to 300 lux band.

sources.title: Wang 2020 blue versus red
sources.detail: Hao Wang et al., Transcriptomic profiling sheds light on the blue-light and red-light response of oyster mushroom (Pleurotus ostreatus), AMB Express 10 (2020). Blue LED 430 to 470 nm at about 50 umol/m2/s improved cap growth. Red 610 to 640 nm did not.
